meaning: The root رَحَقَ (raḥaqa) carries a single sense in the classical lexica. Ibn Fāris records it as كلمة واحدة — one word — الرَّحِيق, a name for wine, and said to be the finest of it: unmixed and smooth to swallow.
en_note: Statistically derived from translation co-occurrence, not a lexical definition. Highlighting only.
meaning_previous: The root رَحِيقٌ (raḥīq) primarily refers to the finest, purest, or most excellent wine, often described as unadulterated and easy to swallow. It can also denote a type of perfume or honey.
meaning_source: Derived from the classical dictionaries (chiefly Maqayis al-Lugha, Ibn Faris d.1004) held in lexicon_full/
